title: Diagnostic & improvement plan
subtitle: Diagnose a pattern, then make a plan
objectives: Collect comparable samples across language skills.
Distinguish recurring errors from isolated slips.
Set a measurable improvement goal without claiming a certified level.
warmup: Retrieve two sentences and one repair strategy from c4-u12. Change the subject or situation in each sentence and explain what changed. Then read today’s objectives and predict where your existing language may be insufficient.

lectures.title: Un diagnóstico que conserva la evidencia
lectures.body: Reúne una muestra escrita sin ayuda, una grabación de dos minutos, una síntesis de una escucha y una conversación con preguntas imprevistas. Anota las condiciones: tiempo, preparación, apoyos y familiaridad con el tema. No compares una redacción revisada durante horas con una respuesta oral improvisada como si midieran lo mismo. Clasifica dificultades de forma, vocabulario, organización, comprensión e interacción. Un error aislado puede ser un descuido; una pauta que aparece en varias tareas merece atención. Conserva ejemplos exactos y el efecto comunicativo: no basta con escribir “mi gramática es mala”. Ninguna de estas muestras convierte automáticamente tu desempeño en una certificación CEFR.

lectures.title: De la observación al experimento
lectures.body: Elige una prioridad concreta: por ejemplo, mantener claras las referencias cuando narras con varias personas. Define una intervención breve, una nueva tarea y un criterio observable. Puedes revisar dos ejemplos, practicar una reformulación y pedir a un interlocutor que identifique los referentes en otro relato. Si mejora una tarea ensayada pero no una nueva, todavía falta transferencia. Planifica un ciclo de práctica, observación y ajuste; no una promesa de fluidez en una fecha fija. Incluye una dimensión de interacción real cuando sea posible. El trabajo en solitario ayuda a preparar y revisar, pero no sustituye la respuesta a una persona que introduce información inesperada.

reading: En su diagnóstico, Nora escribe un informe claro, pero en una conversación usa ella para dos personas distintas y su interlocutor pierde el hilo. Al escuchar la grabación, detecta el mismo problema tres veces. No concluye que “no sabe hablar”: identifica una dificultad de referencia bajo presión. Su plan consiste en preparar relatos breves con dos personajes, repetir un nombre cuando cambia el sujeto y comprobar si el oyente puede reconstruir la secuencia. La semana siguiente utiliza un tema nuevo. Aunque habla con más pausas, necesita menos aclaraciones sobre quién hizo cada acción. Ese resultado sugiere una mejora específica, no un avance global certificado. También observa que su interlocutor conoce bien el tema; por eso decide repetir la tarea con otra persona antes de generalizar. Redacta un plan equivalente para una dificultad observable en tu propia muestra, o utiliza el caso ficticio si todavía no tienes una grabación.

worked.reason: A self-diagnostic guides learning; it does not constitute official standardized certification.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: The conditions should be comparable.
quiz.explanation: “Las condiciones deben ser comparables” expresses “The conditions should be comparable”. “El interlocutor perdió el hilo” instead means “The interlocutor lost the thread”. “Mi prioridad será la referencia” instead means “My priority will be reference clarity”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: An isolated slip.
options: Voy a comprobarlo en otro contexto
quiz.explanation: “Un descuido aislado” expresses “An isolated slip”. “Anotaré las condiciones de práctica” instead means “I will note the practice conditions”. “Voy a comprobarlo en otro contexto” instead means “I will check it in another context”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: There is evidence of transfer.
options: Ajustaré el plan según la evidencia
quiz.explanation: “Hay evidencia de transferencia” expresses “There is evidence of transfer”. “Necesité menos aclaraciones” instead means “I needed fewer clarifications”. “Ajustaré el plan según la evidencia” instead means “I will adjust the plan according to the evidence”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: The diagnostic does not certify a level.
options: El diagnóstico no certifica un nivel
answers: El diagnóstico no certifica un nivel
quiz.explanation: “El diagnóstico no certifica un nivel” expresses “The diagnostic does not certify a level”. “No puedo generalizar todavía” instead means “I cannot generalize yet”. “Las condiciones deben ser comparables” instead means “The conditions should be comparable”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: The goal should be observable.
options: Conviene que el objetivo sea observable
answers: Conviene que el objetivo sea observable
quiz.explanation: “Conviene que el objetivo sea observable” expresses “The goal should be observable”. “Un descuido aislado” instead means “An isolated slip”. “Mi prioridad será la referencia” instead means “My priority will be reference clarity”.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
answers: ["Conviene que el objetivo sea observable","La dificultad aparece bajo presión","El interlocutor perdió el hilo"]
quiz.explanation: “Conviene que el objetivo sea observable” means “The goal should be observable”. “La dificultad aparece bajo presión” means “The difficulty appears under pressure”. “El interlocutor perdió el hilo” means “The interlocutor lost the thread”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

This is the source model, not a text to submit unchanged. A successful adaptation retains the communicative purpose while changing relevant forms and facts. Compare with the worked examples for the reasons behind form choices.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: fulfills the specified purpose; organized and comprehensible; target forms support meaning; revisions are explained with examples. 0 = no evidence, 1 = substantial help needed, 2 = effective with some support, 3 = independently effective for this task. Record who evaluated the work.

homework.prompt: Complete the resource assignment, or ask a willing reader to read the original text without showing it to you. First listen for the situation and purpose; listen again for three details and one contrast. Write a 60–100-word listening log naming the source, words actually heard, one uncertainty, and how you checked it. If using local synthesized speech, label it synthetic. Text-only preparation is not completed listening.
homework.model: A useful log separates the speaker’s message from your interpretation: “I heard [specific phrase]; I understood [claim]; I was uncertain about [word/relationship]; checking [text or partner] changed my interpretation to [correction].” Use the unit reading as an answer reference for a read-aloud version, never as evidence of an external speaker’s words.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: identifies source and listening conditions; retrieves central meaning; supports three details; checks a specific uncertainty. Do not count a copied transcript as independent comprehension.

homework.prompt: Collect a writing sample, a short recording and a live exchange if available. Create a four-session improvement experiment with a baseline, intervention, new task and observable criterion; document limits.
homework.model: Use the original reading/dialogue and the sentence-pattern cards as preparation. Make a brief outline, then put it away. Your partner should introduce a detail you did not prepare. Respond, request clarification if needed, and summarize what you agreed or still disagree about. Solo fallback: record two possible viewpoints and improvise a response after a pause; label it rehearsal.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task fulfillment, comprehensibility, control of target language, responsiveness to another speaker. A partner or instructor should cite one example per score. Solo rehearsal provides no evidence for live responsiveness; mark that dimension not observed.

homework.prompt: On a later day, retrieve six cards without looking. Use three in a fresh response to the practical task. Identify one recurring form error and one communication difficulty. Produce a corrected example, explain the reason, and schedule a specific follow-up exchange or listening session.
homework.model: Compare your response with these two models: Las condiciones deben ser comparables / Un descuido aislado. A useful reflection explains the function, not just the spelling. Revisit the first worked item and create a different example of its principle.
homework.rubric: Report recall count separately from performance. Reflection is complete when it contains an observed difficulty, an explained correction, a fresh example, and an actionable next session.

task: Collect a writing sample, a short recording and a live exchange if available. Create a four-session improvement experiment with a baseline, intervention, new task and observable criterion; document limits.
culture: A diagnostic should not punish accent identity or a disability-related difference. Define intelligibility and task success in context, and record accommodations so comparisons remain fair.
selfAssessment: I can collect comparable samples across language skills.
I can distinguish recurring errors from isolated slips.
I can set a measurable improvement goal without claiming a certified level.
remediation: Sort mistakes by form, meaning, and interaction. For form errors, explain a worked example and create a contrasting pair. For comprehension errors, replay a short segment or use a willing reader and verify your interpretation. For interaction difficulties, repeat the practical task with one new constraint. Compare evidence across days; repeated selection of a known answer alone is not mastery.
